title: Can tabular Q-learners invade an evolving population of spiking agents?
question: Six of twelve founders, and all their descendants, are driven by tabular Q-learners instead of their spiking networks; bodies, sensors, actions, rewards and reproduction rules are identical. Do Q-learner lineages take over the population, and does it matter whether a newborn inherits its parent's Q-table or starts from zero?
background: Controllers: see neuralmind/research/invasion.py (2048 binarised sensor states, epsilon 0.05, alpha 0.1, gamma 0.9). The 'label' condition marks the same six founder lineages but leaves them SNN-driven, which measures neutral drift of lineage share. An engineering pilot on one unregistered seed (9999, 2000 ticks) showed q_inherit lineages reaching 100% and q_fresh lineages falling to ~3%; these predictions were written after that pilot. The primary metric is the mean share of the population in marked lineages over the whole run (invader_share_mean), which is robust to when fixation happens. Seeds 800-811 have never been run.

hypotheses.statement: Q-learners that inherit their parent's table out-compete SNN lineages (relative to the neutral-drift control)
Q-learners that start every life from a zero table lose to SNN lineages
Neutral-drift control: marked SNN lineages hold about half the population on average
